clue.text: Course like an O.T.C. sort

parts.note: like means as, in the sense of 'in the manner of'

indicators.note: to sort letters is to put them into a new order, so the initials are rearranged

parts.note: the Officers' Training Corps initials, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a training course as being like an Officers' Training Corps sort of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' is the anagram signal. The course meant is a racecourse, the famous one in Berkshire, England, not a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a course, and this Berkshire venue hosts Royal race meetings.

clue.text: Concealed attack from a doctor — caused mistake

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: a mistake garbles things, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An ambush from a doctor came about through an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' is the anagram signal, and MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is the usual crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from hiding; this is its older form.

clue.text: Furniture with many locks

parts.note: C, the roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
locks of hair

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture covered in lots of tresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' means tresses, not fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat for one person is a common piece of furniture.

clue.text: Happen to succeed in investment ?

definitions.meaning: occur
a place bet is won when a horse finishes in the first few, so the bet pays out

explanation.surface: Someone hopes an investment will turn out well.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is racing: a horse that comes second or third has been placed, so an each-way investment pays.
explanation.definitionFit: Events occur, and a horse placed in a race makes a place bet succeed.

clue.text: How underwriters contribute ?

parts.note: read literally, underwriters are those who write under, i.e. sign their names at the foot of a document to pledge money

explanation.surface: A question about how insurance underwriters put money into a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin roots sub (under) and scribere (to write) make the word mean exactly 'write underneath', which is what someone signing a pledge does.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge money by signing your name to a list is to contribute, as underwriters of a share issue do.

clue.text: Sink the coal-carrier

definitions.meaning: to sink a ship on purpose
a lidded metal bucket for carrying coal to the fire

explanation.surface: An order to sink the ship carrying coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately holing a ship sends it down; a coal bucket by the fireplace has the same name.

clue.text: Reports about the foreign ornaments

indicators.note: the noises go about, around, the French article

parts.note: reports are loud noises such as gunshots
le is French for the

explanation.surface: News stories about decorations from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' are explosions, not news; 'about' puts them around the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid bracelets worn on the wrist or arm are ornaments.

clue.text: Space trip garments.?

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Clothing for a journey into space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' is the anagram signal, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeveless cloaks worn round the shoulders are garments.

clue.text: Where we might see the battle centre

definitions.text: Where we might see the battle centre

parts.words: Where we might see the battle centre
parts.note: the centre letters of the word battle are TT, and the TT motorcycle races are held on an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A question about where a war was fought.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'battle centre' is TT, the middle of 'battle'. The Tourist Trophy (TT) motorbike races run on this island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The island is where the TT road races are run every year.

clue.text: Charles's attempt ?

parts.note: Charles Lamb, writing as Elia, is famous for short prose pieces, and the word also means an attempt

explanation.surface: A man called Charles makes a try at something.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb's best-known work is the Elia collection of short prose pieces; the word also means an attempt, as a verb or noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A try at something is an attempt, and Lamb's short literary compositions bear the same name.

clue.text: Polluted water supply for Lancashire town ?

parts.note: filthy, polluted water can be called black
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream, a supply of running water

explanation.surface: A northern town has a problem with its contaminated water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN is the Scottish and northern English word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackburn is a large mill town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Hides stones ?

definitions.meaning: animal skins with the fur on
as a verb, pelting someone means throwing stones at them

explanation.surface: Someone conceals a cache of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words change part of speech: 'Hides' is a plural noun, not the verb, and 'stones' is a verb, to pelt with stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Furry animal skins are pelts, and a person who throws missiles repeatedly at a target pelts it.

clue.text: Waste material for book, perhaps

definitions.meaning: leftover bits thrown away
the word goes in front of 'book' to make a book for keeping cuttings

explanation.surface: A note that waste paper might be used for making a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded leftovers are scrap, and a scrapbook is a book in which cuttings are pasted.

clue.text: Everyone's to enter test ? Don't believe it!

indicators.note: the first pieces go into the word for test, so they enter it

parts.note: to give something a test is to try it
everyone is, contracted, gives all's
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everybody must sit an exam, and the speaker refuses to credit the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone's' stands for 'all is', ALLS; with TO it goes inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbelievable yarn is one you would greet with disbelief.

clue.text: Enliven foreign friend in mountain retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the friend goes inside the mountain

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily
ami is the French word for friend

explanation.surface: A visiting companion livens things up at a hideaway in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountain retreat' looks like a hideaway; 'retreat' reverses ETAMINA (AMI in ETNA).
explanation.definitionFit: To bring life or energy to something is to enliven it.

clue.text: Tramp gets: into trouble carrying much weight

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vagrant gets into difficulty while carrying something heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link but is fodder: TRAMP and INTO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with influence carries much weight, meaning it is significant.

clue.text: Speak badly of the meat Mrs Wild supplies

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something unflattering said about the meat that a Mrs Wild sells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like Mrs Wild's surname, but it signals an anagram of MEAT and MRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stutters and halts over words speaks badly in the sense of without fluency.

clue.text: What a row in London from the guns !

definitions.meaning: A street in Westminster, London
large guns collectively

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the din of guns in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a street name, not a noise: Artillery Row is a street in Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy guns are known collectively by this word, and a London street bears it.

clue.text: Turned up to see about our sets-being repaired

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: things being repaired are put back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone goes to see about getting their television sets fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being repaired' is the anagram signal; the surface suggests fixing radio sets, but the definition is a snub nose's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose that turns upward at the tip is described with this French word.

clue.text: Potentate has written letter to the papers

parts.note: the letter M written out as a word is em
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A ruler sends a letter to the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written letter' is a letter's name spelt out, EM for M.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ruler of an empire is a potentate, a monarch with great power.

clue.text: Part of a platoon or a division

definitions.meaning: a small army unit within a platoon
a part into which something is divided

explanation.surface: A soldier's unit is part of a platoon or a larger division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division' looks like a large army unit, but here it means any part.
explanation.definitionFit: An army platoon splits into small units of this name; any subdivision is also one.

clue.text: Fabric put round a metal

indicators.note: the word for put is placed round the other pieces

parts.note: to put something down is to set it
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: Cloth wrapped around a piece of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal; 'put' supplies letters rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin satin, or one with cotton mixed in, is a fabric.

clue.text: Drink one for the road

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice
a passenger car attached to a motorcycle

explanation.surface: A final drink before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for the road' usually means a last drink, but here it is a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocktail and the motorcycle attachment share the name.

clue.text: Impudent — hardly describes some modern youths

definitions.meaning: shameless and cheeky
read literally, the word means having a bare, unbearded face, which bearded young men do not

explanation.surface: Cheeky youngsters of today are hardly described by this word.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a face that is bare, without a beard, which hardly fits bearded young men.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameless cheek is barefaced impudence; literally the word means clean-shaven.

clue.text: Space shot at the start of the race

definitions.meaning: an empty gap

definitions.text: shot at the start of the race
definitions.meaning: a cartridge with no bullet, fired from the starting pistol

explanation.surface: A rocket launch is the start of the space race.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the space race; the start of a running race is signalled with a starting pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty space is a gap, and a starter's pistol fires bulletless cartridges.

clue.text: Trust a sporting body to hit out !

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports authority is relied upon to strike back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief and confidence in someone is trust.

clue.text: What a dance ! How low can you get?

definitions.text: What a dance ! How low can you get?

parts.words: What a dance ! How low can you get?
parts.note: a Caribbean dance in which performers lean back to pass under a bar that is lowered each round

explanation.surface: Exclamations at an outrageous dance and a question about sinking so low.
explanation.walkthrough: The dancers ask how low they can get as the bar drops; the word also means a state of neglect, the lowest place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinidadian dance is judged by how low a dancer can pass beneath the bar.

clue.text: Omens obscure ? Just a particle

indicators.note: obscured letters are hidden in a jumble, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad signs are unclear; one is only a tiny thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' rearranges OMENS; 'Just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle made of a quark and an antiquark.

clue.text: Violin-maker appears in the morning, very early

parts.note: a.m. is the abbreviation for the morning hours
at one, written AT I with roman numeral I, is a very early hour

explanation.surface: A craftsman of fiddles turns up at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the morning, very early' is read as 'a.m., at I', one o'clock in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were famous Italian makers of violins.

clue.text: Grows untidy ?

definitions.meaning: gets bigger
split into two words, the answer means having creases in it, so crumpled

explanation.surface: Something becomes messier as it gets bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN CREASES, the word means crumpled.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow is to become larger; clothes that are crumpled are untidy.

clue.text: Great War soldier needs room to about turn:

parts.note: a kitchen is a room in a house

indicators.note: about turn is the drill command to face the other way, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A First World War soldier needs space to perform an about-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses RE to ER. Lord Kitchener was the British war secretary on the famous recruiting poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Field Marshal Lord Kitchener led Britain's war effort as war secretary in the First World War, until he drowned in 1916.

clue.text: Novelist gets some money on German book

annotationWithheld.why: Novelist gets some money on German book (5), YONGE: Y (yen) + ON + G leaves E unexplained for 'book', and no standard parse gives the last letter
annotationWithheld.clue: Novelist gets some money on German book
